small_guidance:
- Add `triton.autotune` over (BLOCK_OC ∈ {32, 64}, BLOCK_HW ∈ {32, 64, 128}, num_warps ∈ {4, 8}, num_stages ∈ {2, 3}) for the conv kernel; current 32×64 with 4 warps likely under-utilizes the SMs at H_o*W_o=225.
- Hoist the per-(kh,kw) validity masks and the `ih*W+iw` index computation out of the IC loop (they don't depend on ic) and load weights for all OC×IC at once per (kh,kw) via a 2D tile to amortize the gather; also try swapping loop order so IC is the innermost contiguous-stride dimension.
- For group_norm with HW_o=225 (rounded BLOCK=256), CPG=16 → tile is 16×256 = 4096 elements per program, fine; try num_warps=8 and ensure the load uses a 2D contiguous-channel layout (already does). Consider fusing GN with the pool kernel's epilogue since each program already computes a full (oc-tile, hw-tile).
large_guidance:
- Redesign as an im2col-style GEMM: treat the transposed conv (stride=1) as a regular conv with flipped kernel (already done) and tile (OC × output_pixels) as the GEMM M×N, with K=IC*KH*KW. Use `tl.dot` on BLOCK_M=64, BLOCK_N=64, BLOCK_K=32 tiles instead of the current outer-product accumulation across 4 pool positions — this maps better to tensor cores and removes the explicit 4×duplicate accumulators.
- Switch to NHWC (channels-last) input layout so the GEMM-K (IC) axis is contiguous; do a one-time layout transform of x and weight in forward. This makes weight loads and input gathers coalesce along IC.
- Fully fuse: a single persistent kernel per (N, OC_tile) that streams across spatial tiles, computes conv+BN+tanh, performs the 2×2 max-pool reduction in registers, accumulates GroupNorm statistics (sum, sum-of-squares) per group across spatial tiles, then does a second pass (or uses on-chip storage of the pooled tile) to apply normalization — eliminating the separate GN kernel launch and the pooled tensor round-trip to HBM.
